title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Internal Tools (People Ops Guide)
author: Asha Mehta
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical People Ops handbook entry for new and existing employees at Redwood Inference. It summarizes what it means to work here, our role and career ladder structure, benefits and perks, an end-to-end hiring and onboarding overview, and the internal tools you will use daily. Owners and points-of-contact are included for operational sections.

== 1. Working at Redwood — culture & expectations ==

Intro: Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on delivering production-grade LLM inference. We value craftsmanship, clear ownership, measured risk-taking, and empathy for our customers and colleagues. This section summarizes cultural norms and day-to-day expectations.

- Mission alignment: Ship features and improvements that improve latency, reliability, and unit economics for customer workloads.
- Communication: Prefer asynchronous docs and proposals for non-urgent work. Use RFCs/PRDs for cross-team changes.
- Decision-making: Default to documentation and explicit owners; use ADRs for long-lived architecture decisions.
- Meetings: Keep meetings outcome-oriented with an agenda and clear next steps.
- Inclusion: We expect respectful behavior, with psychological safety to raise concerns. See People Ops code of conduct for details.

Owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai)

== 2. Roles & career ladders ==

This section explains role families, expectations at each level, and promotion criteria. Each product/engineering manager should link to team-specific ladders in their onboarding packet.

=== Role families ===

- Engineering: Backend, Serving Runtime, Infra, Platform, SRE, DX/SDKs.
- Applied ML: Model Onboarding, Evals, Quantization Profiles.
- Product: PM, Product Design, Data Product.
- Go-to-market: Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering.
- People Ops, Finance & Legal, Security & Compliance.

=== Typical ladder (engineering example) ===

1) IC-1 / New grad
- Scope: small tasks with mentor oversight.
- Expectations: shipping small bug fixes, readable code, participating in design reviews.

2) IC-2 / Mid
- Scope: owning small services/components, clearly scoped projects.
- Expectations: end-to-end ownership, code quality, mentoring interns.

3) Senior / IC-3
- Scope: cross-service features, performance/latency improvements.
- Expectations: design leadership, measurable impact (e.g., 15-30% throughput improvement), mentorship.

4) Staff / IC-4
- Scope: multiple components or a critical service; influence on architecture.
- Expectations: drive technical strategy, lead cross-team initiatives, publish ADRs.

5) Principal / IC-5+
- Scope: company-wide technical leadership.
- Expectations: long-term platform decisions, hiring and developing leaders.

=== Promotion criteria (summary) ===

- Evidence-based: promotions require documented impact, manager and peer reviews, and calibration.
- Typical timeline: 12-24 months between levels depending on role and impact.
- Process: Manager initiates (promotion packet) -> reviews by calibration committee -> People Ops validates comp and title changes.

Owner: People Ops & Engineering Leadership

== 3. Benefits & perks ==

Redwood offers a competitive benefits package. Below is a high-level summary; detailed plan documents live in the Benefits portal and with HR.

=== Core benefits ===

- Health: Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple tiers and HSA options.
- Time off: 20 days PTO baseline + public holidays; flexible parental leave policies.
- Retirement: 401(k) with company match up to 4%.
- Equity: Standard employee equity grants with refreshers tied to performance review cycles.

=== Perks and wellbeing ===

- Learning stipend: $1,200/year for conferences, training, books.
- Home office stipend: One-time $600 and ongoing reimbursement for ergonomic equipment.
- Commuter / Transit plan where regionally applicable.
- Quarterly company hack days and speaker series.

=== Special programs ===

- Care leave: up to 8 weeks paid for primary caregivers in addition to parental leave (policy details HR).
- Mental health: confidential counseling sessions and mental health apps subscriptions.

Owner: People Ops & Finance (benefits@redwood.ai)

== 4. Hiring & onboarding overview ==

This section describes the hiring stages, interview design, candidate experience standards, and the new-hire onboarding checklist.

=== Hiring stages & interviewer guide ===

1) Sourcing & screening
- Recruiter screens for role fit and basic qualifications.
- Hiring manager confirms technical baseline or product fit.

2) Interview loop
- Standard loop: Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager screen -> Technical (pairing or take-home) -> Cross-functional/team interview -> Hiring manager debrief.
- Core expectations: use scorecards, standardized rubrics, and calibrated benchmarks to reduce bias.

3) Offer & background checks
- Offers are approved by People Ops and Finance. Background checks initiated after verbal acceptance.

Owner: Recruiting & Hiring Managers

=== New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days) ===

1) Pre-boarding (1-7 days before start):
- Complete paperwork in HR portal.
- Set up accounts (Okta), hardware order placed, Slack invite sent.

2) Day 1-7:
- Orientation: company intro, People Ops walkthrough, benefits enrollment window opened.
- Team: meet direct manager, buddy assigned, initial 1:1 cadence scheduled.
- Tools: access to internal dashboards, repo readme and code-of-conduct.

3) Month 1:
- Deliverable: small onboarding project or bug to become familiar with codebase.
- Checkpoint: 30-day manager review and feedback session.

4) Month 2-3:
- Deliverable: larger scoped feature or infra change with code review and release.
- Checkpoint: 90-day performance review and final onboarding acceptance.

Owner: People Ops & Hiring Team Leads

== 5. Internal tools & how to get access ==

This section lists the primary internal systems, recommended onboarding order, and quick how-tos for common tasks. Access requests follow our standard access-and-permissions policy.

Recommended onboarding order: Okta -> Slack -> Google Workspace -> GitHub -> CI/CD dashboard -> Internal Console (deploys/observability) -> Finance & Benefits portals.

=== Key systems ===

- Okta (SSO)
  - Use to access all company services. For MFA, enable push-based authenticator.

- Slack
  - Primary communication. Join channels: #all, #eng, #people-ops, specific team channels. Use status and do-not-disturb during deep work.

- GitHub (repos)
  - Branching model: feature/*, fix/*, release/*; PRs must include a description, tests, and link to related ticket.
  - Code review expectations: at least one approving review for non-trivial changes, 2+ reviews for cross-team changes.

- CI/CD dashboard (internal)
  - Pipeline naming conventions: service-name/main, service-name/staging.
  - Rollback: use the Console rollback feature; see runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/rollback-playbook.

- Internal Console (deploys, observability)
  - Use for release rollouts, health dashboards, tracing links, and cost breakdowns per route.
  - Alerting: on-call SREs receive P1 alerts; use incident process for escalations.

- HR & Benefits portal
  - Enroll in health plans within 30 days of start date; submit expense reports here.

- Finance systems (expense, payroll)
  - Submit expenses within 60 days. Expense tags: travel, hardware, training. See finance-and-legal/expense-policy.

=== Access requests & security ===

- All access requests go through Okta group provisioning or ServiceNow ticket for exceptions.
- For elevated access (production deploy, KMS/HSM), complete the Justification form and receive approval from team lead and security.

Quick CLI snippets and examples: (put in repo: docs/internal-tools/quickstart)

1) Git clone and initial repo setup

$ git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/service-name.git
$ cd service-name
$ ./scripts/bootstrap.sh

2) Deploy to staging (Console CLI)

$ console auth login --sso
$ console deploy service-name --env staging --tag my-feature-branch

=== Troubleshooting common problems ===

- Cannot access repo: verify Okta login and GitHub SSO group membership; if missing, open a ticket to access-requests@redwood.ai.
- CI failing on lint: run ./scripts/lint locally and fix reported issues.

Owner: Eng Platform & People Ops

== 6. Frequently asked questions (FAQ) ==

Q: How do I request a transfer between teams?
A: Talk to your manager and People Ops; complete the internal mobility form. Transfers require manager approvals from both teams.

Q: What is the parental leave policy?
A: Base parental leave is 14 weeks fully paid; contact benefits@redwood.ai for region-specific details.

Q: Who do I contact for workplace accommodations?
A: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai).
